name: Yuhmu, otomí de Ixtenco
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 7 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: [p. 18 n. 2] En el otomí en general, y esto mismo se retomó para el yuhmu, solo se escribe el tono que recae en la sílaba acentuada. [p. 55] El yuhmu es una lengua tonal, es decir, los hablantes usan la altura musical de su voz para generar un cambio en el significado de las palabras. El yuhmu, como las demás variedades de otomí habladas en otras regiones, tiene tres tonos: uno alto en el que la altura de la voz es aguda, uno bajo en el que la altura de la voz es grave y, por último un tono ascendente, que empieza en la voz grave y va subiendo poco a poco hasta alcanzar una voz aguda. [p. 56, after Cuadro 61: Khú̠ni 'barba' / Khù̠ni 'masa' / Nikhǔ̱ni 'metate'; Tshógi / Tsògi / Tsǒgi] Como pudiste notar, en estas palabras la única diferencia se debe a la característica aguda, grave o ascendente que tiene el tono en la primera sílaba (la primera sílaba en otomí es la que está más a la izquierda de la palabra, en otomí la importancia del tono se manifiesta principalmente en esta sílaba, por ello es que solo se escribe el tono en ella). En el caso de la palabra metate, resulta interesante mencionar que la primera sílaba ni- no cuenta para recibir el tono diferenciador, sino que en este caso es la sílaba khǔ̱. Revisando el trabajo de la profesora Yolanda Lastra (1997), ella registró la palabra metate en la voz de don David Alonso como khǔ̱ni. [...] Por ello, pensamos, como ya se mencionó, que ni- no es la sílaba que recibe el tono en esta palabra.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: [p.55] Yuhmu is a tonal language, i.e. speakers use the musical pitch of the voice to change word meaning. [...] it has three tones [...] [p.56] in these words the only difference is the high, low or rising quality of the tone on the first syllable (the first syllable in Otomi is the leftmost one of the word; in Otomi the importance of tone shows mainly on this syllable, which is why tone is written only there). [...] the first syllable ni- does not count for receiving the distinguishing tone [...] [p.18 n.2] In Otomi generally, and this was adopted for Yuhmu, only the tone that falls on the accented syllable is written.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (98-page InDesign PDF with text; PDF page number = printed page number) and extracted pp. 18, 55-58 with extracted text. All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: p.18 fn.2 'En el otomí en general, y esto mismo se retomó para el yuhmu, solo se escribe el tono que recae en la sílaba acentuada.'; p.55 Introducción 'El yuhmu es una lengua tonal, es decir, los hablantes usan la altura musical de su voz.. tiene tres tonos: uno alto.. uno bajo.. un tono ascendente'; p.56 after Cuadro 61 (Khú̠ni/Khù̠ni/Nikhǔ̱ni; Tshógi/Tsògi/Tsǒgi) 'la única diferencia se debe a la característica aguda, grave o ascendente que tiene el tono en la primera sílaba (la primera sílaba…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ixtenco Otomi is described as a three-tone language (H, L, LH); the tone-bearing 'accented' syllable is the first syllable of the word, i.e. the stem/root-initial syllable (a prefix-like syllable such as ni- in ni-khǔ̱ni 'metate' is skipped), and only that syllable is written with tone. This amounts to root-/stem-initial prominence carrying the lexical tone contrast; no independent stress rule or acoustic evidence for stress is given.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Ixtenco. (Pan-Otomi: Guerrero Galván 2015: 257 and 2013: 497 report a secondary accent on the third syllable / on words with more than one foot, but not on Ixtenco data.)
new_statements.exceptions: Prefix-like initial syllable ni- (nikhǔ̱ni 'metate', also recorded by Lastra 1997 as khǔ̱ni) does not carry the distinguishing tone; proclitic articles/possessives Rà 'the' vs Rá 'his/her' contrast by tone on their own (p. 57, Cuadro 62).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms (isolated nouns/verbs with audio); 'primera sílaba' refers to the leftmost syllable of the lexical word excluding prefixal ni- and proclitics, i.e. effectively the root-initial syllable. Pedagogical orthography manual co-authored by a native speaker and an INAH phonetician; the authoritative description (Lastra 1997: 21-25) was not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: Yuhmu = otomí de San Juan Bautista Ixtenco, Tlaxcala = Ixtenco Otomi, glottocode ixte1237, ISO otz (the manual's data are from co-author M. I. E. Yonca Gaspar, native speaker of Ixtenco, with reference to Lastra 1997's consultant David Alonso). The stronger accent statements found (Guerrero Galván 2013, 2015: accent obligatorily on the root, secondary accent on a later foot) are pan-Otomi generalisations based mainly on Santiago Mexquititlán Otomi (Querétaro; mezq1235-area northwestern Otomi), not on Ixtenco, and should not be entered under ixte1237.

sources.note: Ch. III 'Los tonos' (pp. 55-58): yuhmu is tonal with three tones (alto, bajo, ascendente); the tonal contrast is carried by the first syllable of the word ('la primera sílaba en otomí es la que está más a la izquierda de la palabra.. la importancia del tono se manifiesta principalmente en esta sílaba'), a prefix-like syllable such as ni- in nikhǔ̱ni 'metate' does not count; p. 18 fn. 2: tone is written only on 'la sílaba acentuada'. No further explicit stress rule; no acoustic discussion of stress.

sources.citation: Guerrero Galván, Alonso. 2015. Patrones tonales y acento en otomí. In Esther Herrera Zendejas (ed.), Tono, acento y estructuras métricas en lenguas mexicanas, 235-260. México: El Colegio de México. Open access:https://repositorio.colmex.mx/concern/books/6682x683c
sources.note: Pan-Otomi study (acoustic data from Santiago Mexquititlán Otomi); Ixtenco appears only in the phoneme-inventory tables sourced from Lastra (1997: 21-25). Conclusions (pp. 257-258): accent is demarcative and falls obligatorily on the root (left edge of the radical); words with more than one foot get a secondary accent; basic trochaic pattern; correlates are duration and intensity; the three tonal contrasts occur only in the tonic syllable; Otomi characterised as 'tono-acentual'. Not an Ixtenco-specific statement.
